rationale: A view bound to a value channel has to know when the channel went quiet, so a meter can fall back to its neutral instead of freezing on its last reading when audio stops. Staleness cannot be derived from the value: a compressor holding a steady -6 dB of gain reduction publishes the same number every block and must keep reading -6, while a processor whose audio stopped publishes nothing and must decay. Comparing values cannot distinguish those two, so the sources now carry the fact a reader actually needs. One transferred surface moves with it: value_source.hpp gains a PublishCounter base that MeterSource, VectorSource and ScalarSource inherit, holding a monotonic std::atomic<uint32_t> incremented in publish(). The store is relaxed because the counter orders no other memory — it only has to be monotonic and eventually visible on the reader thread — so the audio-thread publish path stays alloc-free and non-blocking exactly as before. No existing member, signature or buffer layout changes; publish() and read() keep their semantics and the TripleBuffer payloads are untouched. This is Pulp-specific plugin-UI capability work with no counterpart framework behaviour to backport.
